notable_absence.predicate: n/a - contradicts an existing closed-set assumption rather than absenting one
notable_absence.finding: The registry currently holds backup:full-backup and backup:incremental-backup as the only two promoted backup-type concepts, with no note that a third exists. cbbackupmgr-info.md's own EXAMPLES section shows a third value directly in the tool's real output - 'Name | Size | Type | Complete | Retention | Expiry State' rows showing 'FULL', 'INCR', and, after a merge, 'MERGE - FULL' - and states in prose: 'the type which can be either a full backup (FULL), and incremental backup (INCR) or a merge (MERGE).' Treating backup type as a two-member closed set (as the registry implicitly does by only having promoted the first two) would be wrong; backup:merge-result is minted here to fill the gap. Separately, the JSON output schema documents its own internal deprecation - 'Note that the "range" and "merged_range" fields contain the same data. The range field is included for backwards compatibility but is deprecated' - a clean retainedForLegacyCompatibility candidate, but with no version attached to when the deprecation happened, so it could not be tied to deprecatedIn without inventing a date.

cross_component_finding: This page's --start/--end range-selection logic is the one that later determines whether a merge will include a full backup ('When I merge with this range, will it include a full backup?') - i.e. info's read-only reporting function is a documented prerequisite step for using the merge command correctly, even though info itself performs no merge. This is a workflow dependency between two commands (info -> merge) that neither page's own OPTIONS/SYNOPSIS section states as a formal requirement; it only appears in the worked EXAMPLES prose. Relevant to whichever sibling batch record extracts cbbackupmgr-merge.md.
cross_product_finding: The info command's own note that S3-stored archives can be queried without downloading the whole archive ('This will download a very minimal amount of data e.g. it won't download the whole archive') is the same non-Capella, cloud-object-store-as-target pattern flagged in cbbackupmgr-cloud.md - reinforcing that cbbackupmgr's 'cloud' vocabulary means AWS/Azure/GCP object storage as an archive location, never Capella as a target service, which remains a separate axis with no source stating a correspondence.
